results.question: What is the waiting period for pregnancy?
results.answer: It's 12 months. The mother needs to have served this waiting period before Medibank can pay towards hospital admissions for pregnancy and birth services, regardless of the due date or whether she was already pregnant when taking out or upgrading cover. Please check your Cover Summary to confirm your cover includes Pregnancy and birth services.

results.question: What is the waiting period for a pre-existing condition on hospital cover?
results.answer: It's 12 months for treatment of a pre-existing condition (PEC) on hospital cover. The exceptions are psychiatric care, rehabilitation and palliative care, which have a two-month waiting period even if the condition is pre-existing. Pregnancy and birth services always have a 12-month wait. Medibank's Medical Practitioner decides whether a condition is pre-existing, based on a PEC certificate from your doctors.

results.question: How long do I wait before I can claim general dental on extras?
results.answer: Usually 2 months. General dental falls under "All Treatment", which has a two-month waiting period, while major dental (like endodontics, surgical extractions and orthodontics) has a 12-month wait. No benefits are paid for services received during a waiting period. Check your Cover Summary for the waiting periods on your cover.

results.question: Can I suspend my membership while I travel overseas?
results.answer:
Yes, you can suspend your membership for overseas travel if you meet these conditions:
• Apply before you leave.
• You must be away for at least two months (maximum four years).
• No benefits are paid for anything during the suspension, and it won't count towards waiting periods.
• You may have to pay the Medicare Levy Surcharge while you're suspended.

results.question: Is there a cooling off period if I change my mind after joining?
results.answer:
Yes, you have 30 days from the date your new or changed cover starts to review it. If you change your mind in that time and haven't made any claims, you can:
- switch to a more suitable cover from the original start date, or
- cancel and get a full refund of premiums paid.
You generally can't move back to a cover Medibank has closed.

results.question: How far in advance can I pay my premiums?
results.answer: Generally up to 12 months in advance for any cover. If you have standalone Ambulance Cover, you can only pay either six or 12 months in advance. Medibank may refuse or refund any payment that would take your cover more than 12 months ahead of the payment date.

results.question: How long do I have to submit a claim after my treatment?
results.answer: You have two years from the date of service (or the date you bought the item) to submit a claim. Claims lodged after that won't be paid. Benefits are based on the cover you held on the date of service.

results.question: If I switch from another health fund, do I have to serve waiting periods again?
results.answer:
Generally no, as long as you join Medibank within two months of leaving your previous fund. You'll usually only serve waiting periods for:
- treatments not covered by your old policy
- higher benefits (e.g. upgraded services or bigger annual limits)
- any waiting periods you hadn't finished
A break of more than two months means all waiting periods apply. Check your Cover Summary.

results.question: Is ambulance covered by my hospital or extras cover?
results.answer:
Usually yes – Medibank pays benefits towards ambulance services under most Hospital and Extras covers. If you're in NSW or the ACT with Hospital cover, a government ambulance levy is included in your premium, so send any ambulance account to Medibank to forward for payment.
Check your Cover Summary to confirm your cover.

results.question: What is a benefit replacement period?
results.answer: A benefit replacement period is a set time you need to wait from the date you bought an item before you can get another benefit to replace it. It's separate to the item's waiting period, and can apply per member or per membership depending on your cover. Check your Cover Summary to see which items have one.

results.question: How do I add my newborn baby to my membership?
results.answer:
Contact Medibank to add your baby, ideally from their date of birth. Timeframes to backdate cover to birth:
- Single membership: within 2 months (you'll move to a family or single parent family cover and pay higher premiums from the birth date)
- Couple or family membership: within 12 months
Your membership must have started no later than the birth date.

results.question: What is Lifetime Health Cover loading?
results.answer: It's an extra amount added to your Hospital cover premium if you didn't hold hospital cover by 1 July after your 31st birthday (your LHC base day). It's 2% for each year you're aged over 30 when you take out cover, up to a maximum of 70%. The loading is removed once you've held hospital cover and paid it for 10 continuous years.

results.question: How do I make a claim for extras?
results.answer:
The easiest way is to use your membership card for electronic claiming at the provider, then just pay the remaining balance. If that's not available:
- Claim online through your My Medibank account
- Or post a claim form (download it at medibank.com.au) with original receipts, keeping a copy

Some items may need supporting documents.

results.question: What happens if I fall behind on my premium payments?
results.answer:
You can't claim benefits for any services or items you get while your premiums are behind. To get back on track:
- Pay all outstanding premiums (as agreed with us), plus the minimum advance premium
- If you're more than two months behind, your membership may be closed without notice
- If it's closed, we may reinstate it at your request once all premiums are paid

results.question: What does the accident waiting period waiver mean?
results.answer: It means that if you have an Accident during a one-day or two-month waiting period on your Hospital cover, Medibank may waive that waiting period for treatment resulting from the Accident. All other waiting periods still apply. To claim, submit an Accident form (download it at medibank.com.au). An Accident is an unforeseen event caused by an external force, needing immediate treatment.

results.question: What about for extras like dental?
results.answer:
It depends on the type of dental work. Under Medibank Private extras, general dental falls under the standard two-month waiting period, while these have 12 months:
- Endodontic (root canal) treatment
- Surgical extractions and procedures
- Orthodontics
- All major dental services
Check your Cover Summary for the waiting periods on your cover.

results.question: I'm expecting a baby in a few months, when will my cover pay for the birth?
results.answer: Only once the mother has served a 12-month waiting period on cover that includes Pregnancy and birth services. This applies regardless of your due date or whether you were already pregnant when you took out or upgraded your cover. So if you joined or upgraded only a few months ago, the birth admission may not be covered. Check your Cover Summary to confirm it includes Pregnancy and birth services.

results.question: My friend get diagnose with breast cancer after she joined medibank for 1 year, will she be covered?
results.answer: Likely yes, if her cover includes the treatment she needs. After 12 months of cover, both the general two-month waiting period and the 12-month pre-existing condition waiting period for hospital treatment would have been served, so a pre-existing condition assessment shouldn't apply. This assumes she hasn't upgraded her cover in the last 12 months. She should check her Cover Summary to confirm what's included.

results.question: My mum has had a bad hip for years. If she joins now, can she get a hip replacement straight away?
results.answer:
No, probably not straight away. If her hip symptoms existed in the six months before she joins, it's likely to be treated as a pre-existing condition, which has a 12-month waiting period.

- Medibank's Medical Practitioner decides this, using a PEC certificate from her GP and specialist.
- If she's treated as a private patient during the waiting period and it's a PEC, she'd pay all hospital and medical charges.

Check her Cover Summary.
